newsitem.title: NORWAY: Storebrand helps lift Norwegian stock.
newsitem.headline: Storebrand helps lift Norwegian stock.

text.p: Norwegian shares closed higher with trade focused on Storebrand on Wednesday following the release of 1996 profits of Norway's biggest insurance company.

The Oslo Bourse Total index rose in brisk morning trade before activity tapered off in the afternoon. The index finished 0.29 percent higher at 1,079.40 points in turnover of 1.1 billion crowns, including 89 million in Storebrand.

"The market calmed down after a lot of trading," one dealer said. "There was a bit of profit-taking in Storebrand and a general self-correction. The dollar for a while was very strong against the crown, but then weakened."
"I think the market will be a bit flat in the next few days," he said.
The Total index trade chart largerly followed that of Storebrand, which jumped more than four percent only to close 1.10 percent higher at 46 crowns.
Storebrand's profits beat market expectations and there was talk that an investor may seek to take control of the company.
"The result surprised the market but the price is also up because of speculation on what is happening with Storebrand," one dealer said.
